A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Residual Deep Gaussian Processes on Manifolds. Their complete main texts, equations, figures and appendices are readable and support matching retained content across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic regression, Bayesian optimisation, ERA5 wind interpolation and UCI regression experiments in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds extended-depth tests, deep-only Bayesian optimisation and a further wind-model comparison in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The residual Gaussian-vector-field/exponential-map architecture, inducing-location and interdomain variational families, and Appendix B extension are retained. New Appendix C explains the existing construction through its relationship to wrapped GPs; it does not introduce a different proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic sphere functions, irregular and Ackley optimisation tasks, 2010 ERA5 wind data and five UCI datasets. Added depth configurations and optimisation schedules retain this coverage. The inconsistent altitude captions in v2 Figures 15–16 do not establish additional altitude coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix A.5 adds the Section 4.1 Euclidean-hidden-layer baseline to wind interpolation, adapted with a coordinate-frame GVF output, and evaluates it in Figures 15–16. v1's wind comparisons contain only shallow and deeper Hodge models. The other original comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: New experiments extend depth from five to ten layers and run Bayesian optimisation with a deep GP from the first iteration, using output-layer hyper-priors and L-BFGS. Appendix A.4 also revises the original optimiser description from Adam generally to Adam for deep models and BFGS for shallow models. Equation (28) corrects the lattice longitude formula. These reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Figures 9–10 test depth sensitivity and saturation through ten layers. Figure 12 tests removing the initial 180-iteration shallow-GP stage and displays unsuccessful deep-only runs. These substantially extend v1's five-layer analysis and staged optimisation experiment by examining depth robustness and dependence on initialisation.

E5.justification: The additional ten-layer comparisons report ten randomised runs, whereas the retained synthetic comparisons report five. This is a separate expanded analysis, not evidence that every original experiment received more runs. Standard-deviation bands and the original Bayesian optimisation, monthly wind and UCI reporting practices remain.

E6.justification: v2 adds depth curves showing early performance plateaus, wind comparisons showing lower Hodge NLPD with largely similar MSE, and deep-only optimisation outcomes. Appendix A.4 reports improvement over the shallow GP in 12 of 15 runs, often before iteration 100, while three runs remain trapped in local minima. These are additional results; the original main-text and UCI result plots are retained.

T1.justification: Equation (28) corrects the mathematical grid definition by changing longitude from 2πn/φ to 2πi/φ. The Euclidean-data mapping's sphere dimension is also corrected to S^d while retaining the same normalisation formula. The substantive GP and covariance derivations, including Appendix B, remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and central method and application claims remain unchanged. The conclusion adds an explicit claim that increasing depth virtually never degrades performance but can quickly saturate, together with a hypothesis that larger datasets would require more layers. This is a limited extension of the earlier robustness claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.4 adds a substantial account of optimisation variability, relating it to the initial observations near the optimum. It interprets deep-only optimisation as potentially more sample-efficient but more vulnerable to local minima, and identifies exact-versus-sparse inference and BFGS-versus-L-BFGS as possible confounds. The conclusion additionally discusses depth saturation and its possible dependence on dataset size.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 explicitly documents variational-parameter counting formulas. Appendix A.4 discloses hyper-prior use for the original shallow model and its absence for the original deep models, while Appendix A.5 specifies the new baseline's coordinate frame and Matérn 5/2 kernels. The code-availability statement and existing hardware information are retained.

R1.justification: v1 briefly mentions Mallasto and Feragen's wrapped GPs; new Appendix C explains their connection to the proposed layers and distinguishes manifold inputs, identity base points and sparse inference. This is a focused expansion of positioning relative to an already cited work. The Azangulov reference's publication update represents the same work.

P1.justification: v2 makes local language corrections, updates the publication header and first author's affiliations, expands appendix explanations and adds Appendix C. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact, so this is not an extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: The appendix gains five figures covering extended depth, deep-only optimisation and wind baselines, substantially expanding its visual evidence and rearranging retained plots. The swapped MSE/NLPD captions in v1 Figures 10–11 are corrected in v2 Figures 13–14. However, new Figures 15–16 introduce altitude-caption inconsistencies with their panel labels. Main-text figures and wind maps are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful additional checks on depth, optimisation initialisation and wind-model comparisons, while documenting failures and clarifying its relationship to wrapped GPs. Formula corrections and implementation disclosures also improve reproducibility. These are targeted gains to an already supported contribution: the new optimisation comparison changes several settings simultaneously, limiting causal interpretation, and the new wind captions introduce inconsistencies.
